test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 28 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Three candidates contested in an election and received 1036, 7044 and 12,120 votes, respectively. What percentage of the total number of votes did the winning candidate get?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **winning candidate** by the maximum votes: 12,120.

Total votes = 1,036 + 7,044 + 12,120 = 20,200.

Winning % = (12,120 ÷ 20,200) × 100.

Winning % = 12,120 ÷ 202 = 60%.

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Votes of **Candidate 1** = 1,036

Votes of **Candidate 2** = 7,044

Votes of **Candidate 3** = 12,120

**Formula Used:**

Percentage = (Component Value ÷ Total Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f47079a949efe847dcf5532e6ae9aeb857ad5af7ee6503c6996b46cbad2ab1e6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total number of votes = 1,036 + 7,044 + 12,120

⇒ Total number of votes = 20,200

⇒ Votes of winning candidate = 12,120

⇒ Winning percentage = (12,120 ÷ 20,200) × 100

⇒ Winning percentage = (12,120 ÷ 202) = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Calculation

To find what percentage X is of Y, use the base formula: (X ÷ Y) × 100.

Vote Difference

The **margin of victory** is calculated as the difference between the votes of the winner and the runner-up.

Valid vs Invalid Votes

Total votes cast = Valid votes + Invalid votes. Percentages are usually calculated on **valid votes** unless stated otherwise.</p
